Cement Masons and Plasterers

OPCMIA — Operative Plasterers' and Cement Masons' International Association

OPCMIA Local 300 cement mason and plasterer apprenticeship as a training body; ACI concrete field testing and cold weather concreting guidance; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart Q concrete and masonry construction and 29 CFR 1926.1153 respirable crystalline silica

Eight ways a slab, a curb, a wall or a floor gets closed right: struck off and troweled, power-finished under guard, formed and finished at the curb, built in three plaster coats, shot from a nozzle, cut wet, coated and ventilated, and protected through a freeze — cement burns, silica, guarding and fumes named on every one.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1590lessons across the track
120tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Construction & Structural Trades

Slab Screed, Bull Float & Trowel

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

A slab on grade closed the way OPCMIA teaches it: struck off across checked rails, floated once, hand-troweled after the bleed water leaves, and cured before the crew signs off.

  • ACI — ACI 302 - Guide for Concrete Floor and Slab Construction
  • ACI — ACI concrete field testing technician certification and ACI 301 specifications for structural concrete
  • union — OPCMIA Local 300 - cement masons and plasterers apprenticeship, as a training body
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926 — Safety and health regulations for construction
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.1153 — Respirable crystalline silica in construction
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.701 — Concrete and masonry construction, general requirements

What it proves

Competency: Place, finish and protect concrete and plaster to the specification, never to the clock

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 8 stations, against OPCMIA OPCMIA Local 300 cement mason and plasterer apprenticeship, as a training body; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart Q Concrete and masonry construction; OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1153 Respirable crystalline silica; ACI ACI 306 Guide to Cold Weather Concreting.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: OPCMIA Local 300 cement mason and plasterer apprenticeship as a training body; ACI concrete field testing and cold weather concreting guidance; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart Q concrete and masonry construction and 29 CFR 1926.1153 respirable crystalline silica. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
